goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose, only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
`weed check` is the primary face: it judges the index plus the working tree against HEAD by default (what pleach's smoke gate sees after it stages a worker's files), `--staged` judges the index alone (the pre-commit face), `--base <ref>` judges the tree against a ref (CI). It prints SARIF when stdout is not a terminal and a table when it is, `--format` overrides, and it exits 0, 2 or 3 as the contract says. `weed rules` prints the catalogue. The git seam lives here, and the first rule runs end to end: G1, conflict markers.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/check-face.tend2.html) is your full context, read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) with no flags weed judges index plus working tree against HEAD, `--staged` judges the index only, and `--base <ref>` judges the tree against that ref, proven on a temp repo carrying a distinct change in each zone · evidence expected at: tests/check_scopes.rs
- (code) exit 0 on a clean diff and on warnings only, 2 with at least one block-level result, 3 outside a git repository, on an unknown ref, and on a malformed `weed.toml`, each with one stderr line naming the cause · evidence expected at: tests/check_exit.rs
- (code) SARIF on stdout when it is not a terminal, a table when it is, and `--format` overrides both · evidence expected at: tests/check_format.rs
- (code) G1 fires at block level on conflict markers at line start (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) in each of ts, py, rs and go through the real binary, and stays silent on a neighbour that carries `=======` inside a string and a markdown table rule · evidence expected at: tests/rule_g1.rs
- (code) `weed rules` prints every rule with id, default level, face and one-line finding, and the levels match `Config::default()` · evidence expected at: tests/rules_catalogue.rs
- (code) `--strict` reports a suppressed block finding at its original level and exits 2, while without `--strict` the same diff exits 0 with the finding as a note · evidence expected at: tests/check_strict.rs
- (code) `examples/pleach/plan.json` declares `"accept": { "smoke": "weed check --strict" }` and passes `pleach validate`; `docs/pleach.md` explains that weed sees the staged files plus the tree against HEAD, so no base argument is needed · evidence expected at: scripts/check/pleach-example.sh

## Definition of done, verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/check-face.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload a6e4ccfe99f8 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 default mode chosen from pleach's own gate: `accept.smoke` runs in the node worktree after scoped staging, exit-code gated, no arguments passed (`~/conductor/workspaces/pleach-v1/cayenne/src/loop/run-node.ts`, the smoke block)
- 2026-09-05 G1 lands here, not in rules-block, so the pipeline is proven end to end by the simplest rule before the catalogue is built on it
- 2026-09-05 the CLI is `clap` with derive; subcommands for scan, guard, bite and hook are added by their own loops, each in its own file under `src/faces/`
- 2026-09-05 the fixture harness moved here from core's Tried: core delivered no `tests/common/mod.rs`, and this is the first loop that needs one

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file, check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green, it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Probe/scratch files (toolchain checks, experiments) go in `.loop-scratch/` only, it is never collected; scratch files elsewhere pollute the delivery.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root, what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
